nodes.label: Postgres Performance Optimization Guide
nodes.author: supabase
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive Postgres performance optimization guide for developers using Supabase and Postgres. Contains performance rules across 8 categories, prioritized by impact from critical (query performance, connection management) to incremental (advanced features).

nodes.label: Use Connection Pooling for All Applications
nodes.norm_label: use connection pooling for all applications

nodes.label: Use Prepared Statements Correctly with Pooling
nodes.norm_label: use prepared statements correctly with pooling

nodes.label: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout
nodes.rationale: Idle connections waste resources and hold locks. Setting idle_in_transaction_session_timeout to 30s reclaims 30-50% of connection slots from idle clients.

nodes.label: max_connections Sizing
nodes.rationale: Too many connections exhaust memory (1-3MB RAM per connection) and degrade performance. Set limits based on available resources to prevent database crashes.

nodes.label: PgBouncer Connection Pooling
nodes.rationale: Postgres connections are expensive (1-3MB RAM each). Without pooling, applications exhaust connections under load; connection pooling handles 10-100x more concurrent users by sharing a small pool of connections.

nodes.label: Prepared Statements with Transaction Pooling
nodes.rationale: Prepared statements are tied to individual database connections. In transaction-mode pooling, connections are shared across requests, causing prepared statement does not exist errors unless unnamed statements, deallocation, or session mode is used.

nodes.label: Row Level Security (RLS)
nodes.rationale: Database-enforced tenant isolation ensures users only see their own data, preventing accidental data leaks from application bug or bypass.

nodes.label: RLS Column Indexing
nodes.rationale: Always create indexes on columns used in RLS policies to prevent full table sequential scans.

nodes.label: Enable Row Level Security for Multi-Tenant Data
nodes.norm_label: enable row level security for multi-tenant data

nodes.label: Principle of Least Privilege
nodes.rationale: Grant only minimum required permissions to application roles; never use superuser, revoke default public privileges, and separate readonly and writer roles.

nodes.label: Cached RLS Subquery Pattern
nodes.rationale: Wrapping auth.uid() in (select auth.uid()) evaluates the function once per statement instead of once per row, running 100x+ faster on large tables.

nodes.label: Security Definer Helper Function Pattern
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER functions bypass RLS for membership lookups but must explicitly verify caller identity with auth.uid() and revoke execute from public roles.

nodes.label: Batch INSERT Statements for Bulk Data
nodes.norm_label: batch insert statements for bulk data

nodes.label: Eliminate N+1 Queries with Batch Loading
nodes.norm_label: eliminate n+1 queries with batch loading

nodes.label: Use Cursor-Based Pagination Instead of OFFSET
nodes.norm_label: use cursor-based pagination instead of offset

nodes.label: Batch INSERT Operations
nodes.rationale: Individual INSERT statements incur high network and transaction overhead. Batching multiple rows in single statements yields 10-50x faster bulk inserts.

nodes.label: Batch Loading to Eliminate N+1
nodes.rationale: N+1 queries execute one query per item in a loop. Batching them into a single query using arrays or JOINs yields 10-100x fewer database round trips.

nodes.label: Cursor-Based Pagination
nodes.rationale: OFFSET-based pagination scans and discards all skipped rows, getting progressively slower on deeper pages. Cursor/keyset pagination provides consistent O(1) performance regardless of page depth.

nodes.label: Atomic UPSERT with ON CONFLICT
nodes.rationale: Using separate SELECT-then-INSERT/UPDATE creates race conditions under concurrency. INSERT ... ON CONFLICT provides an atomic operation that eliminates race conditions.

nodes.label: Identity Primary Key
nodes.rationale: SQL-standard sequential bigint identity primary key provides optimal index locality and compactness for single-database workloads.

nodes.label: UUIDv7 Primary Key
nodes.rationale: Time-ordered UUIDv7 preserves B-tree locality without causing page fragmentation in distributed databases.

nodes.label: Optimal PostgreSQL Data Types
nodes.rationale: Reduces storage by 50% and improves performance: bigint for IDs, text over varchar, timestamptz for time, numeric for currency, boolean for flags.

nodes.label: UUIDv4 Index Fragmentation Anti-Pattern
nodes.rationale: Random UUIDv4 primary keys scatter inserts across the entire B-tree, causing severe cache invalidation and page splits.

nodes.label: Idempotent Constraints Migration Pattern
nodes.rationale: Postgres does not support ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS; use DO block checking pg_constraint before adding to ensure safe, repeatable migrations.

nodes.label: Foreign Key Indexing
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL does not automatically index FK columns; missing indexes cause 10-100x slower JOINs and full table scans on CASCADE deletes.

nodes.label: Composite Index
nodes.rationale: Single composite index is more efficient than combining multiple single-column indexes via bitmap index scan.

nodes.label: Covering Index
nodes.rationale: Include non-searchable columns via INCLUDE clause enabling index-only scans without heap fetches.

nodes.label: BRIN Index
nodes.rationale: Block Range Index is 10-100x smaller for large time-series tables where data is naturally ordered on disk.

nodes.label: B-Tree Index
nodes.rationale: Default index type optimal for equality and range operators (=, <, >, BETWEEN, IN, IS NULL).

nodes.label: GIN Index
nodes.rationale: Generalized Inverted Index optimal for array containment, JSONB queries, and full-text search.

nodes.label: GiST Index
nodes.rationale: Generalized Search Tree optimal for geometric data, range types, and nearest-neighbor (KNN) queries.

nodes.label: Hash Index
nodes.rationale: Equality-only index slightly faster and smaller than B-tree for exact match lookups.

nodes.label: Partial Index
nodes.rationale: 5-20x smaller indexes, faster writes and queries by only indexing rows matching a predicate.

nodes.label: Table Partitioning
nodes.rationale: Splits tables >100M rows by range into monthly partitions; queries only scan relevant partitions and old data can be dropped instantly via DROP TABLE.

nodes.label: Leftmost Prefix Rule
nodes.rationale: Column order matters: place equality columns first and range columns last to maximize query coverage.

nodes.label: JOIN Column Indexing
nodes.rationale: Indexing referencing columns on foreign keys prevents full table scans during joins.

nodes.label: WHERE Clause Indexing
nodes.rationale: 100-1000x faster queries by avoiding sequential scans on frequently filtered columns.

nodes.label: Concrete Transformation Patterns
nodes.rationale: Show exact SQL rewrites. Avoid philosophical advice.

nodes.label: Error-First Structure
nodes.rationale: Always show the problematic pattern first, then the solution. This trains agents to recognize anti-patterns.

nodes.label: Quantified Impact
nodes.rationale: Include specific metrics to help agents prioritize fixes.

nodes.label: Self-Contained Examples
nodes.rationale: Examples should be complete and runnable. Include CREATE TABLE if context is needed.

nodes.label: Snake Case Lowercase Identifiers
nodes.rationale: Postgres folds unquoted identifiers to lowercase. Snake_case unquoted identifiers prevent case-folding errors and avoid required quoting in tools and ORMs.

nodes.label: Advisory Locks
nodes.rationale: Efficient coordination without row-level lock overhead; eliminates need for dummy locking rows.

nodes.label: Use Advisory Locks for Application-Level Locking
nodes.norm_label: use advisory locks for application-level locking

nodes.label: Prevent Deadlocks with Consistent Lock Ordering
nodes.norm_label: prevent deadlocks with consistent lock ordering

nodes.norm_label: keep transactions short to reduce lock contention

nodes.norm_label: use skip locked for non-blocking queue processing

nodes.norm_label: postgresql select for update skip locked documentation

nodes.label: Consistent Lock Ordering
nodes.rationale: Eliminates deadlocks by explicitly acquiring locks in consistent ID order before updating.

nodes.label: Minimal Transaction Scope
nodes.rationale: Hold locks only for the actual database update to maximize throughput and avoid blocking on external API calls.

nodes.label: SKIP LOCKED Queue Pattern
nodes.rationale: Non-blocking parallel worker job processing by skipping locked rows.

nodes.label: Index JSONB Columns for Efficient Querying
nodes.norm_label: index jsonb columns for efficient querying

nodes.label: tsvector Full-Text Search
nodes.rationale: LIKE with wildcards cannot use standard indexes and scans all rows. Full-text search with tsvector is orders of magnitude faster (100x faster than LIKE) and supports ranking.

nodes.label: JSONB Indexing Pattern
nodes.rationale: JSONB queries without indexes scan the entire table. Using GIN indexes for containment queries yields 10-100x faster JSONB queries.

nodes.label: jsonb_path_ops Operator Class
nodes.rationale: Supports only the @> containment operator, but creates a 2-3x smaller index compared to the default jsonb_ops.

nodes.label: Supabase CLI Best Practices
nodes.rationale: Always run --help for command syntax discovery; use execute_sql or db query for live iteration without polluting migration history.

nodes.label: Data API Table Exposure
nodes.rationale: Newly created SQL tables may not be automatically accessible through PostgREST Data API without explicit GRANT SQL to anon and authenticated roles.

nodes.label: Supabase Debugging Guidelines
nodes.rationale: Consult official Monitoring and Debugging documentation when encountering API, database, or service errors rather than retrying blindly.

nodes.label: Supabase MCP Server Troubleshooting
nodes.rationale: Diagnostic sequence: server HTTP reachability, .mcp.json presence, OAuth 2.1 authentication flow, and token permissions.

nodes.label: Auth and Session Security Policy
nodes.rationale: raw_user_meta_data is client-editable and unsafe for authorization in RLS; raw_app_meta_data must be used instead, and session revocations must be validated.

nodes.label: Row Level Security Rules
nodes.rationale: Enforce RLS in all exposed schemas. auth.role() is deprecated in favor of TO role; ownership predicate is mandatory to prevent BOLA; UPDATE requires both USING and WITH CHECK.

nodes.label: Scoped Personal Access Tokens Policy
nodes.rationale: Never use classic full-account PATs in scripts, CI, or agents; scoped tokens limited to targeted organizations and projects should be used instead.

nodes.label: Security Definer Functions Guidance
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER bypasses RLS and is callable by PUBLIC by default; prefer SECURITY INVOKER or isolate function in a non-exposed schema with auth.uid() checks.

nodes.label: Query Plan Diagnostics
nodes.rationale: Diagnose slow queries using actual timings, buffer reads, and row filter counts instead of guessing.

nodes.label: Autovacuum Tuning
nodes.rationale: Tuning vacuum and analyze scale factors on high-churn tables prevents stale statistics and bloat.
